chapter_title: Concerning Wisdom; it is far superior when on the
spiritual_reading:
When a person is admitted into interior discernment and receives living truth within the inmost will, and then fixes it in the formed teaching of the understanding, there arises a deep gladness from conjunction. Yet the delight is greater when that inward discernment is brought forth into use, and given form in outward expression; for then it enlightens the whole person more fully, and what was inward becomes manifest, and by that manifestation truth is strengthened and power for life is taken up.

I perceive that what has been expressed is sound. I know that the discernment I have received has been diffused through my inner life and ordered in my whole spirit. Yet it does not seem to me to stand forth in its full brightness, as something advanced and complete, unless it is brought out into actual expression and communicated to others. For when I bring it forth, I am giving it into the reception of another’s understanding. Would I have been moved toward it with such desire, and would my affection have been drawn to it as it is now, if it had remained only hidden within and never come to me as something to be received and shared? Teach me why discernment becomes more fully developed when it is expressed in act, than when it is held inwardly in fixed form.

You ask well. The instruction you seek is great, and from it comes the gladness felt in expressing discernment. For discernment is more fully alive in outward expression than in inward retention alone. You yourself rejoice when you bring it forth; and the one who receives it from you rejoices as well, is enlightened by it, and through that enlightenment is confirmed into enduring strength.

For it is as when a new life of good is first formed within the affection that receives it. It stirs within that affection and fills the interior state, so that the receiving love perceives and knows that a living beginning is present. There is a joy over that hidden formation until the time when it comes forth into open life. Then what was within is brought into free activity, complete in its powers according to its kind, and appears without disorder, in a more open and spacious state of life than before. It is then filled with wisdom’s light and speaks from living understanding, as one who has been brought into a new degree of life.

At the first formation within, the joy is not so great as when the formed life comes into open operation and is clearly seen at once in its quality and measure. Then love and joy are multiplied far beyond what they were while it was only inwardly held.

For while it was being formed within, its quality and its clear perception were concealed from the receiving love; but when it comes forth into open life, its quality is seen. Its measure and its pleasantness come plainly before the perception of both the will and the understanding, and before all things in the person that are related and conjoined. Joy increases as it is more directly perceived in its true form and delight.

In the same way, discernment present within the will is like a living beginning of new life held within affection. When a person is taught and fixes it inwardly, it is like a life being prepared to come forth, which will then be seen in its quality.

So discernment, when it is brought forth into expression from within, is elevated more and more. Its increase and its manifested excellence are multiplied from the time its inner beauty and brightness are presented to the understanding of those who receive it. And it advances also within the one who expresses it, because the bringing-forth opens reception anew, and the speaker then perceives with wonder what has been given to be expressed.

Again, discernment is like this while it remains hidden within. Before it is brought forth, it is like love’s ardor held inwardly within the natural degree, present there as potency but not visible as wisdom. The natural degree can be disposed by that inward ardor, yet the radiance that is within it does not appear. Many such natural knowledges and forms can be gathered together within one external life, and yet that life cannot be enlightened by them so long as the inward light within them is not released into clear understanding. But when they are joined to living love and thus opened, illumination goes forth from them; and a whole external life can be enlightened from a single opened truth.

So it is with discernment held within the will. It is like inward love whose illumination is not yet displayed. In itself it is living, yet its light and excellence are hidden in the interiors; but when a person brings it forth into expression and communication, its excellence is made manifest before the perception and reception of many.

For in this respect discernment is like that new life of good brought into open operation. When it comes forth, everything in the person that is conjoined with it rejoices. Yet there are also states that are not conjoined which are distressed because of it, since they have no kinship with it. These are not numbered among its related affections and thoughts. They do not rejoice in it because it is not of their quality.

So it is with discernment when it is expressed by one who teaches. Those who are in agreement with it in affection and understanding receive it and rejoice in it; but those who are not in agreement with it are strangers to it, and neither rejoice in it nor admit it.

It is like illumination that becomes manifest outwardly for all who are able to perceive it. Whoever is in the capacity of understanding sees that illumination when it has gone forth into clarity; but whoever is in the deprivation of understanding does not perceive it.

So it is with discernment when it is expressed. The one who has the inner faculty of understanding formed within receives it whenever it is heard, because discernment belongs to that formed faculty. But the one who lacks that faculty is a stranger to it: such a one neither admits it nor truly attends to it.

fills.notes: The contrast required is between inward sealing and outward utterance. The substrate idiom regularly speaks of joy increasing or being doubled when truth passes from interior containment into exterior use.
The clause contrasts inward possession with outward proclamation; the minimal restoration that matches the sense is “proclaim it.”
A discourse marker is demanded: the speaker affirms internal perception that the uttered word is right, preparing the request for instruction.
The reply must introduce the causal ground of the increase: wisdom becomes more alive in utterance and in reception by another. A short causal lead-in fits the impersonal teaching register.
The simile requires a sign of animation: the child’s turning is evidence of life within, corresponding to the stirring of a formed life within affection.

The advance ‘for you’ is explained by the speaker’s renewed opening in the act of bringing-forth; in the natural wording this is best carried by joy and wonder as the immediate affectional correspondences of utterance.
The example requires plurality: many woods gathered into one house correspond to many natural knowledges collected in one external life.

fills.fill: the wood does not come forth
fills.notes: The constraint is that illumination cannot occur while the inner light remains unmanifest; thus the missing clause must deny emergence of light from the stored wood prior to joining it to fire.

fills.fill: nor are they enlightened by it
fills.notes: In the substrate logic, rejoicing and enlightenment go together as effects of kinship with wisdom; strangers neither rejoice nor receive, therefore the missing member parallels ‘rejoice’ with ‘be enlightened.’

assessment: Most lacunae are trivial letter restorations. The few substantial gaps are tightly constrained by the correspondential structure: inward sealing versus outward manifestation, the childbirth simile of concealed formation versus open life, and the fire-in-wood image of hidden potency versus released illumination. Where exact phrasing is not recoverable, restorations were kept minimal and in the impersonal cosmological-teaching register of the oldest layer.
